To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the gender difference in depressive symptomatology emerges in adolescence and that it is due to an interaction of cognitive vulnerability and stressful life events.

(a) cognitive vulnerability factors, such as attributional style, dysfunctional attitudes, and self-blaming, are important in understanding the gender difference in adolescent depression, (b) the cognitive vulnerability factors are more important in understanding the emergence of the female preponderence in depression during adolescence than the number and type of stressful life events that adolescents encounter during this period of development, (c) the gender difference in cognitive vulnerability factors is not simply a function of the number of negative life events that adolescents experience

(1) the emergence of the female preponderances in depression during adolescence may be explained by a transactional process in which negative life events, cognitive vulnerability, and depression are interrelated; and (2) the transactional process may be mediated by the development of gender role socialization and gender identity.

how cognitive and social development may be involved in the emergence of the female preponder- ance in depression.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the gender difference in adolescent depression is due to a transactional stress model, in which the causal chain begins with the occurrence of negative events, and then proceeds through generic vulnerability and self generated dependent negative events.

there is a gender difference in depression, that this difference is due in part to the greater exposure of girls to stress and in part to their greater cognitive vulnerability, and that the cognitive vulnerability is due in part (perhaps primarily) to their greater exposure to stressful events.
the gender difference in adolescent depression is a function of the interaction of generic cognitive vulnerability factors and stressful events.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the development of the female preponderances in depression begins with the emergence of the cognitive vulnerability factors that are associated with depression in adulthood.
the gender difference in the incidence of depression begins to emerge at about age 13.
the gender difference in adolescent depression is due to the interaction of generic cognitive factors and the unique socialization experiences of boys and girls.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the gender difference in the prevalence of depression is not simply the result of a gender difference in exposure to negative life events.
the gender difference in the incidence of depression is not a simple reflection of the fact that women are exposed to more negative events than men.
the development of the female preponderances in depression is not a mystery.
